Validated versus provisional

Weather-first boat forecasts

The Dolphin forecast uses a regularized nonlinear model with 15 observed weather/ocean fields, AM/PM, and three lagged encounter-state measures. It contains no date, month, day-of-year, or seasonal predictor. For every Dolphin validation day in 2025–2026, the model is freshly trained on all earlier Dolphin trips; that day remains unseen.

When another boat is selected, BiteCast transfers the validated Dolphin weather pattern by shifting it to that boat’s recent 12-trip AM/PM encounter level. This keeps weather as the day-to-day driver, but the transfer and its displayed ranges are provisional and not independently validated.

Dolphin MAE
Dolphin RMSE
Dolphin within ±2.0

Dolphin range calibration: signed actual-minus-forecast residuals create asymmetric 50% and 80% ranges. Each validation range uses only earlier errors; its 80% band captured of later outcomes.

Freshness policy

How the model stays current

Run a scheduled refresh once daily after dock totals normally settle. The refresh should re-read the latest 14 report days (so late corrections are captured), merge records by a stable source-row fingerprint, refresh NOAA observations and the NWS seven-day grid, retrain the model, rerun the chronological backtest, and rebuild this static page.

Publishing guardrail: deploy only when the scraper succeeds, historical row counts do not unexpectedly shrink, forecast inputs are recent, and the validation report is complete. A transferred forecast should remain labeled provisional until that boat passes a separate rolling-origin test.

Icon treatment

The fish illustrations are original inline vector motifs inspired by the compact side-profile card style in the user’s reference image. They do not reuse the copyrighted FishDatabase artwork shown on the source site. Barracuda, Bluefin, Bonito, Calico Bass, Dorado, Sand Bass, Skipjack, Yellowfin, and Yellowtail receive species-specific color/body treatments; every other species uses a generic fish mark.
